CLEARANCE REQUIRED FOR START: No

CLEARANCE TYPE: Secret

TRAVEL: Yes, 10% of the Time

Description

Our pioneering and inventive spirit has enabled us to be at the forefront of many technological advancements in our nation's history - from the first flight across the Atlantic Ocean, to stealth bombers, to landing on the moon. We look for people who have bold new ideas, courage and a pioneering spirit to join forces to invent the future, and have fun along the way. Our culture thrives on intellectual curiosity, cognitive diversity and bringing your whole self to work — and we have an insatiable drive to do what others think is impossible. The Launch and Exploration Division has an opening for a Mechanical Technician 3 to join our team. This position will be located at Vandenberg Space Force Base, California.

Preferred previous aerospace or military experience in the following:

·       Hands-on operations of large, small, and fragile, ESD-sensitive electronics

·       Mixing and application of adhesives and ablative materials

·       High-pressure pneumatic and hydraulic control systems

·       Ordnance handling, assembly, and test

·       Overhead crane operator

·       Proficient use of various mechanical tools

·       Proficient with forklifts, man lifts, and heavy equipment

·       Proficient with calibrated measuring devices, multi meters, micrometers, calipers, and torque wrenches.

·       Familiarity with preventative maintenance and lockout-tagout practices

Additional Requirements:

  • Serve as an integration and test technician in support of DoD and Space Force programs.  Effectively support operations in-plant and at launch sites.

  • Perform integration and test operations during all phases of a vehicle build, from delivery of the motor case through payload encapsulation and final launch.

  • Adhere to and read established policies and procedures pertaining to job safety and security

  • Adhere to and read technical drawings and work plans/procedures

  • Strong attention to detail

  • Must be willing and able to work occasional odd shifts and extra hours

  • Ability to engage in an environment of continuous product and process improvement

  • High integrity and strong work ethics

  • Flexible and able to deal with multiple tasks simultaneously

  • Calm under pressure

  • Excellent communicator one on one or in group setting

  • Productive time management

  • Able to collaborate and effectively work in a team-oriented environment

  • Gain and continuously maintain technical training and expertise to perform multiple vehicle production activities to include, but not limited to, composite layup and repair; adhesive bonding of structures and standoffs of various substrates; match drilling; riveting and fixture fabrication; harness and RF cable layout, routing, and troubleshooting; connector population; J-STD-001 soldering, ordnance handling, and mechanical assembly

  • Participate in, and periodically serve as the Test Conductor, for hazardous operations, including lifting, ordnance, and high pressure pneumatic/hydraulic operations

  • Mentor work activities of junior technicians

  • Uphold and champion safety and quality assurance policies, procedures, and controls to ensure products and services meet or exceed company standards

  • Some traveling may be required

  • Able to obtain and maintain a DoD Security clearance or SCI Access

 

Northrop Grumman offers a competitive and robust benefits program. As a full-time employee of Northrop Grumman, you are eligible for:

  • Medical, Dental & Vision coverage

  • 401k

  • Educational Assistance

  • Life Insurance

  • Employee Assistance Programs & Work/Life Solutions

  • Paid Time Off

  • Health & Wellness Resources

  • Employee Discounts

Flexible Schedules: For example, some roles offer the ability to work a 9/80 work schedule, which allows an employee to work a nine-hour day Monday through Thursday and take every other Friday off of work.

Basic Qualifications:

  • High School diploma or equivalent and 4 years additional education and/or related experience

  • Experience in handling chemicals such as Isopropyl Alcohol and Acetone

  • Adept at reading drawings, process specification, and work order instructions.

  • Able to obtain and maintain a DoD Security clearance or SCI Access.

  • Willing to work any shift.


Preferred Qualifications:

  • AA degree or other two-year technical degree

  • Familiar with Northrop Grumman Corporation processes.

  • Basic knowledge of Microsoft Office to supplement work order and other data requirements

  • Able to perform daily work in an approved integration processing facility, to include wearing ESD smocks, ordnance jackets, and other PPE.

Primary Level Salary Range: $66,600.00 - $111,000.00

The above salary range represents a general guideline; however, Northrop Grumman considers a number of factors when determining base salary offers such as the scope and responsibilities of the position and the candidate's experience, education, skills and current market conditions.

Depending on the position, employees may be eligible for overtime, shift differential, and a discretionary bonus in addition to base pay. Annual bonuses are designed to reward individual contributions as well as allow employees to share in company results. Employees in Vice President or Director positions may be eligible for Long Term Incentives. In addition, Northrop Grumman provides a variety of benefits including health insurance coverage, life and disability insurance, savings plan, Company paid holidays and paid time off (PTO) for vacation and/or personal business.

The application period for the job is estimated to be 20 days from the job posting date. However, this timeline may be shortened or extended depending on business needs and the availability of qualified candidates.
